title: Models and migrations
summary: Define an inventory model with bounded fields, a readable label, and a migration path.

scenario.briefing: The campus store is moving its inventory into Django. The first model must use field types that match the data: bounded text for names, exact decimals for prices, and an integer quantity with a default.

objectives.description: Apply the taught syntax in a working file.

hints: Keep the class declaration and change the field types.
CharField takes max_length; DecimalField takes max_digits and decimal_places.
Return self.name from __str__ so the admin shows the item name.
Run makemigrations after the model matches the lesson.

misconceptions.feedback: Binary floating point cannot represent every decimal exactly. DecimalField keeps money exact.

misconceptions.description: Expecting migrate to create migration files.
misconceptions.feedback: makemigrations writes the files; migrate applies them to the database.
Without __str__, Django prints Item object (1). Return a readable name instead.

sections.title: A model describes a table
sections.body: A subclass of `models.Model` maps to one database table. `CharField(max_length=120)` bounds text, `DecimalField(max_digits=8, decimal_places=2)` stores exact money values, and `IntegerField(default=0)` supplies a default for new rows.

sections.title: Migrations record schema changes
sections.body: `python manage.py makemigrations inventory` writes migration files that describe the change. `python manage.py migrate` applies them. Commit migration files with the model change so every environment builds the same schema.

steps.title: Define an inventory model
steps.prompt: Edit models.py. Define Item with a CharField name, a DecimalField price, an IntegerField quantity, and a readable __str__. Run the checks when done.

files.content:
from django.db import models


class Item(models.Model):
    name = models.TextField()
    price = models.FloatField()
    quantity = models.IntegerField(default=0)

    # TODO: use a bounded name, an exact price, and a readable label
    def __str__(self):
        return self.name

tests.description: The name uses a bounded character field.
The price uses an exact decimal field with two places.
The quantity is an integer with a default.
The model renders a readable name.

steps.title: Model fields and migrations

statements.label: Each model field becomes a column in the model's database table.
makemigrations applies pending schema changes to the database.
DecimalField stores exact decimal values, while FloatField stores binary floating point.
__str__ provides a readable label for the model in the admin and shell.
CharField can be declared without a maximum length.

steps.explanation: A model maps to a table, and each field maps to a column with a type and constraints. makemigrations writes migration files; migrate applies them. DecimalField is the safe choice for money, and __str__ gives rows a readable label.
